summary: Theo refuses to end the shift because he knows something is buried beneath the trench. Vark assumes obsession until the drill strikes an impossible surface and Theo recognizes it before anyone can explain what they have found.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Wide establishing panel. Olyria-Prime trench at shift end: black bedrock, heavy drill, work lamps, ladders, tired crew clearing out. Theo remains at the rig after everyone else has begun leaving.
Panel 2 — Vark comes down toward Theo expecting an overtime argument. Keep the worksite geography clear and make Theo's refusal to stop feel anxious rather than rebellious.
Panel 3 — Medium two-shot for the opening exchange through 'You said that an hour ago.' Vark is practical; Theo is distracted by the ground beneath them.
Panel 4 — Tight alternating reactions for 'There's something under us.' / 'There is rock under us. That's the job.' Theo cannot explain his certainty without exposing the dream.

Panel 5 — Close on Theo as he admits, 'I've seen what comes next.' Vark asks if he means the survey; Theo says no. Let the work lamps and drill vibration make the moment uneasy without supernatural effects yet.

Panel 6 — Large final panel. The drill strikes something that does not sound like stone; lamps flicker; a dark manufactured surface begins emerging from black bedrock. Theo says 'That's it.' End on Vark realizing from Theo's face that he already knew it was there.

summary: At Zenith Spire, Rae watches a location official history erased reappear in the archive beside a forbidden REDLIN reference. She hides it from Caelum beneath ordinary paperwork and realizes the record is returning rather than being newly created.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Tall establishing view inside Zenith Spire Archives. Ordered architecture, controlled institutional light, long planetary view. Rae works alone at a secure desk; make her dark worn practical silhouette stand out clearly against the brighter ordered archive.

Panel 2 — Insert on the archive interface as an erased Olyria-Prime location begins writing itself back into the record. A restricted line appears clearly and exactly: REDLIN PROTOCOL. Rae recognizes the word emotionally without understanding it.
Panel 3 — Caelum enters and asks, 'What happened at Olyria-Prime?' Rae keeps her body between him and the returning record and answers from the ordinary report.

Panel 4 — Two-shot for 'I didn't ask what the report says.' / 'Then you should ask the people who wrote it.' Rae uses dry irritation as camouflage; Caelum remains controlled rather than melodramatically sinister.
Panel 5 — Close reaction exchange: 'You look ill.' / 'I work nights.' Keep the returning record visible but peripheral, creating dramatic irony.
Panel 6 — Caelum says 'Move.' Rae counters with the freight manifests, physically redirecting his attention with paperwork and blocking the screen without turning the moment into action spectacle.

Panel 7 — Final exchange: Caelum says he wants the screen behind her; Rae answers, 'That's a different request.' End with a quiet final inset after he moves on: the forbidden Olyria entry and REDLIN PROTOCOL remain on the screen. Rae realizes the archive and her dreams are remembering the same erased thing.

summary: Theo touches the Desert Marker and the present is replaced by the last quiet moment before an ancient battle. He sees Starbreaker preparing a catastrophic decisive act, but the memory ends before the act itself. Vark sees only fragments and can no longer dismiss Theo's claims as obsession.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Wide reveal of the Desert Marker exposed in Sector Four. Its wrongness comes from impossible age, scale and deliberate manufacture, not decorative glow. Vark and Theo are small against it.
Panel 2 — Vark draws the practical boundary: nobody touches it. Use the dialogue through 'You dreamed this?' with Vark trying to keep the situation ordinary.
Panel 3 — Theo: 'Every night.' Continue through Vark's 'Good. We agree on something.' Theo removes one glove; his fear should be visible.
Panel 4 — Close on bare palm approaching the Marker as Theo says, 'It makes not touching it impossible.' No explosion. Contact is controlled, geometric and immediate.

Panel 5 — Large memory break. The trench is completely replaced by a ruined ancient battlefield beneath a broken sky in unnatural quiet. STARBREAKER stands at the center as a tired, furious person holding stellar-scale force at the edge of release, using his approved fractured white-gold-black Vanguard design.
Panel 6 — Starbreaker turns toward someone outside frame and says exactly: 'You know what happens if I do.' Do not show the act itself.

Panel 7 — Fragmented return from Vark's point of view: a second sky, impossible figures and a shadow crossing the trench. Make his glimpse partial and disorienting without making him share Theo's full memory.

Panel 8 — Final close panel in the present. Theo is back on the ground, empty hand curled as though it held something; Vark can no longer dismiss him. Theo now carries the name Starbreaker without understanding why.

summary: Adrian finds Theo after the memory rupture. Theo demands validation; Adrian's refusal to look at the Marker reveals that he already knows enough to fear it. Adrian will acknowledge that Starbreaker was real, but not why Theo can remember him.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Establish the damaged excavation tier after the rupture. Theo is injured, dirty and furious; Adrian arrives calm and recognizably the same silver-haired man from the approved modern reference. Adrian deliberately looks at Theo, not at the Marker.
Panel 2 — Theo: 'Tell me you see it.' Adrian: 'I see you bleeding.' Keep the Marker present in composition so Adrian's refusal to look at it is obvious.
Panel 3 — Continue 'Look at it.' / 'I don't need to.' / 'Then you know what it is.' Adrian's control should make the evasion more alarming, not less.
Panel 4 — Adrian: 'I know what follows recognition.' Theo admits he has been seeing the place for years; Adrian corrects him: 'Not this place.'
Panel 5 — Close emotional exchange through 'Since I was a child.' Adrian says, 'Then we're late.' Show the first visible crack in his composure.
Panel 6 — Theo asks exactly, 'Starbreaker was real?' The name lands harder than the accusation. Adrian finally looks shaken.
Panel 7 — Final close on Adrian answering exactly: 'Yes.' One word, no lecture, no added exposition. End on Theo realizing another person recognizes the impossible history.

summary: Rae copies the returning records before they can be erased again. Caelum confronts her, but refuses to answer why the location and Redlin reference were missing from history, confirming that the concealment is institutional rather than accidental.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Rae alone in the secure telemetry room, rapidly copying the material that is returning: erased routes, names, testimony fragments and the REDLIN reference. Keep the information legible as evidence, not decorative hologram clutter.
Panel 2 — Caelum enters or forces access and says, 'Step away.' Rae remains at the terminal: 'I can't.'
Panel 3 — Close two-shot for 'You mean you won't.' / 'No. I mean I can't leave it here.' Their conflict is institutional and personal, not physical combat.
Panel 4 — Caelum invokes Rae's life in the Spire. Rae asks why the place was erased. Show what she stands to lose through the ordered environment around them.
Panel 5 — Caelum demands the drive; Rae demands the name. He answers only 'Rae.' She realizes his refusal is itself evidence.
Panel 6 — Rae: 'You know it too.' She moves toward the door with the copied material; Caelum's control slips for the first time.
Panel 7 — At the threshold Rae says exactly, 'Redlin.' Caelum flinches before he can stop himself. End on Rae seeing that reaction as proof.

summary: While Theo is treated for his injuries, Vark forces him to confront the lie they are about to tell. Their dry, ordinary argument gives way to Vark choosing to protect the discovery from people neither of them trusts.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Human-scale decompression in the field triage tent. Theo on a cot with his injured hand being wrapped by an overworked medic; Vark has a paper incident form because the network is down. Bad coffee and ordinary worker clutter.
Panel 2 — Vark: 'You want me to write chemical fire.' Theo: 'Yes.' Let the absurdity sit in the mundane setting.

Panel 3 — 'There was no chemical fire.' / 'Then make one up.' Include an off-panel worker complaint about a missing boot only as environmental comedy, not as new dialogue lettering unless already scripted.
Panel 4 — Vark's twenty-years line and Theo's retirement-party answer. Use small acting panels; this is deliberately not epic.
Panel 5 — Vark: 'I hate cake.' Theo: 'Vark.' The humor drops away. Vark looks at the damaged hand and remembers what he saw.
Panel 6 — Vark: 'I saw the sky change.' Theo: 'So did I.' Keep both men quiet and credible; no memory imagery is necessary here.
Panel 7 — Final panel. Vark strips identifying information from the incident form and says, 'That's why I'm lying.' His decision is protective, practical and consequential.

summary: Rae searches older records with the stolen drive and finds Adrian already waiting among deliberately sealed histories. He reveals that some history was removed rather than lost, but refuses to tell her why a name from her dreams is returning in the archive.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Establish the lower archives as materially older than the polished Spire: physical books, sealed records, dim controlled light. Rae arrives with the copied material and finds Adrian already there with a sealed volume.
Panel 2 — Rae: 'You're in my archive.' Adrian: 'Not this part.' Their first interaction should feel like two people testing institutional boundaries.
Panel 3 — Rae says exactly, 'Redlin.' Adrian does not answer. Hold a silent reaction beat before continuing.
Panel 4 — Rae: 'You know what's on this.' Adrian: 'Enough to know you should destroy it.' Rae: 'That's convenient.'
Panel 5 — Adrian: 'Convenience has nothing to do with it.' Rae asks why the record was erased. Keep the sealed physical archive material in frame as evidence of deliberate concealment.
Panel 6 — Adrian: 'Because some histories were not lost.' Rae: 'What does that mean?' Adrian: 'They were removed.'
Panel 7 — Rae asks 'By whom?' Adrian answers exactly, 'By people who remembered what happened when they stayed.' End with Rae understanding that the archive's absence is an act, not a gap.

summary: Theo races to hide the Marker before a patrol reaches Sector Four. Adrian watches until Theo's motive changes from proving the object exists to preventing others from possessing it, then quietly helps him conceal it.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Theo returns to Sector Four injured and clumsy, dragging spoil and wreckage over the exposed Marker before an approaching official patrol can arrive. Preserve the Marker geometry and excavation geography from S03.
Panel 2 — Adrian watches without helping. Theo: 'They're coming.' Adrian: 'Yes.' The countdown is visible through distant patrol lights or workers approaching, not an action-movie chase.
Panel 3 — Theo finally says, 'Help me.' Adrian challenges the change in motive: 'You spent years wanting proof.'
Panel 4 — Theo: 'I have it.' Adrian: 'And now?' Theo: 'Now I don't want them to have it.' Make this the emotional hinge of the page.
Panel 5 — Adrian: 'Good.' He immediately joins the concealment effort. Show ordinary physical work: spoil, scrap and collapsed material, not magical hiding.
Panel 6 — Patrol passes close enough to threaten discovery. Adrian uses calm envoy authority to redirect them toward the officially reported collapse.

Panel 7 — Theo: 'You could have helped five minutes ago.' Adrian: 'Five minutes ago you were still deciding what it belonged to.' End with the Marker concealed and Theo understanding that possession, not proof, has become the problem.

summary: Rae chooses to destroy the stolen records rather than let Caelum reclaim them, accepting that the truth now survives only in memory and in what she chose to notice. Caelum's threat confirms that the institution fears remembered meaning, not merely possession of a file.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Quiet Zenith observation deck. Rae waits with the copied material; the ordered city/planetary view contrasts with her precarious position. Caelum approaches without guards or melodrama.
Panel 2 — Caelum: 'You can still give it to me.' Rae: 'And you'll do what?'
Panel 3 — 'What keeps this place standing.' / 'You already erased it once.' Keep Caelum's claim credible enough to be morally difficult.
Panel 4 — 'You don't know that.' / 'Neither do you. That's the problem.' Their conflict is over authority without certainty.
Panel 5 — Caelum: 'Everything you have is here.' Rae: 'No. Everything I have is what I remember.' Make Rae's choice visible in her grip on the copied material.
Panel 6 — Caelum: 'They can take that too.' Rae: 'Then I should leave before they try.'

Panel 7 — Final panel. Rae destroys the copied record using ordinary available disposal infrastructure. Caelum is angry because the knowledge now exists in her rather than in something the institution can seize. Rae leaves.

summary: Theo buries the Marker and confronts Adrian when he discovers the envoy preserved a record of it. Adrian forces Theo to confront that the dangerous fact is not where the object lies, but that something in the forgotten past recognized him.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Abandoned trench after concealment. Theo catches Adrian preserving a small record of the site. Theo has an industrial cutter in shaking hands; the Marker itself remains buried.
Panel 2 — Adrian: 'If you're going to threaten me, point it at me.' Theo: 'I am.' Adrian observes that Theo is actually watching the grave.
Panel 3 — Theo demands, 'Swear you didn't keep the location.' Adrian: 'You still think the location is the danger.'
Panel 4 — Theo: 'What is?' Adrian: 'Recognition.' Give the word space and keep the cutter present but clearly secondary to Theo's fear.
Panel 5 — Theo asks, 'What recognized me?' Adrian answers, 'That's the question.' Theo accuses him of knowing.
Panel 6 — Adrian: 'I know what it resembles.' Theo: 'What?'
Panel 7 — Final close on Adrian: 'A beginning.' No cosmic montage. Let the implication carry the page turn.

summary: Adrian finds Rae after she destroys the archive trail. He helps sever the identity markers that will let the Spire track her and reveals that other people have remembered impossible history before her.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Rae back inside the telemetry/archive system after destroying the copy, now severing the remaining identity trail that connects her to the recovered material. The room should look partially stripped of her institutional life.
Panel 2 — Adrian arrives after the damage: 'You burned it.' Rae: 'You told me to destroy the copy.'
Panel 3 — Adrian: 'I did.' Rae: 'I destroyed the trail.' Make clear that Rae has gone beyond protecting data and has cut herself loose.
Panel 4 — Adrian: 'That was your life.' Rae: 'No. It was my job.' Their difference in age and experience should be visible without paternalism.
Panel 5 — Adrian: 'The distinction matters now.' He breaks or disables the identification crystal the Spire could use to follow Rae.
Panel 6 — Rae: 'Where do I go?' Adrian: 'Somewhere you've never dreamed of.' Rae immediately catches the wording.
Panel 7 — Rae: 'How do you know about the dreams?' Adrian: 'Because you aren't the first.' End on Rae realizing her private impossible experience has precedent.

summary: Theo keeps a fragment from the buried Marker and forces Adrian to admit that he too remembers the forgotten sky. The issue ends with Theo knowing the visions belong to shared history, while Adrian still refuses to say why Theo can remember it.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Night above buried Sector Four. Theo sits alone beneath open stars with his injured hand and a small physical fragment secretly kept from the Marker. Silent machinery and compacted earth establish that the site is hidden again.
Panel 2 — Adrian appears. Theo: 'They said the dreams were mine.' Adrian: 'They are.'
Panel 3 — Theo: 'You know what I mean.' Adrian: 'Yes.' Theo asks whose memory it is. Adrian: 'I can't.'
Panel 4 — Theo: 'Won't.' Adrian: 'Both.' Let the ambiguity remain; do not explain it visually with a lore montage.

Panel 5 — The fragment warms subtly in Theo's injured hand. Theo hears the distant remembered sound of an orbital canopy breaking over a city that no longer exists. Adrian reacts before he can hide it.
Panel 6 — Theo: 'You heard it too.' Adrian: 'Put the shard down.' Theo realizes Adrian knew what the sky sounded like.
Panel 7 — Adrian: 'There are no canopies left to fracture.' Theo: 'But you remember them.'
Panel 8 — Final issue panel. Close on Adrian answering exactly: 'Yes.' Theo's relief that the impossible history is shared is immediately undercut by the realization that Adrian knows why.
